title: Scientists tagged 14,000 endangered Australian moths; not one was found

However, after extensive tracking efforts, none have been recaptured, suggesting potential populations larger than previously assumed. Alternatively, these moths might be utilizing undiscovered migration routes. The ongoing project remains crucial for understanding the ecology of these endangered insects.

title: AI may soon help humans talk to animals and birds

This technology raises ethical questions about animal privacy and potential misuse. Understanding animal signals could lead to manipulation and distress for wildlife. The pursuit of animal communication continues despite these significant ethical considerations.

title: Parents who display kids' achievements may be doing more than showing pride

Furthermore, these displays transform into lasting family mementos that can be cherished for generations.

Authorities are investigating both incidents and promising accountability for those responsible.

title: Mirror donated by spies, Red Fort-sized photos: Why Nasa's new telescope is special

Unlike Hubble, which observed a limited portion of the sky for three decades, Roman will cover fifty times more area. Its sophisticated camera will produce sweeping panoramic images, aiming to transform the landscape of astronomical research and discovery.

title: Space wars are no longer science fiction: How nations are preparing for conflict in orbit

title: J&K: Suspicious movement prompts search ops in Poonch’s frontier villages
content:
Suspicious movement prompts search ops in Poonch’s frontier villages

JAMMU: Security forces launched joint cordon-and-search operations in frontier villages in J&K’s Poonch district on Monday based on inputs about the alleged movement of terror suspects in the area, officials said. “The searches commenced around 12.30pm. Multiple teams are combing the forested upper reaches spanning Jhotian Wali, Dhook Dhoba, and other areas in Mehrote, in Poonch’s Surankote sub-division,” an official said, adding that the operation continued till late Monday. Pertinently, troops of the Army’s 16 RR, 37 RR, and J&K Police’s SOG have been hunting for terror suspects in Surankote since September 2.

title: Detained Pakistan national repatriated via international border
content:
Detained Pak national repatriated via intl border

JAMMU: A Pakistani man detained near the international border in Jammu’s Kanachak sector last week was repatriated on Monday. Troops of BSF’s 44Bn caught the intruder on Sept 3 near a forward area border outpost. During questioning, he identified himself as Nazir Sadhir from Luni Pundra village in Sialkot and allegedly told investigators that he had inadvertently crossed into Indian territory, officials said. Security agencies investigated his claims, following which BSF officials contacted their Pakistani counterparts and initiated the repatriation process. On Monday, Sadhir was handed over to Pakistan Rangers at Golpattan border outpost along the international border after a flag meeting, officials said.

title: National film awards ceremony to be in Gujarat this year
content:
NEW DELHI: A film on the Statue of Unity will be honoured in the shadow of the monument itself when the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony takes place at Ekta Nagar, formerly Kevadia, in Gujarat September 22. Govt has not spelt out the reason for shifting the ceremony out of New Delhi or indicated whether taking the awards to different locations will become a regular practice. The move nevertheless breaks with a long-established pattern. Instituted in 1954, the awards have overwhelmingly been presented in Delhi although University Centenary Auditorium in Madras, now Chennai, hosted the 17th chapter on November 21, 1970. Among those being honoured is filmmaker Aanand L Rai, who won Best Direction in the non-feature category for Statue of Unity - Ekta ka Prateek.

title: Rural area LPG booking period reduced from 45 to 25 days
content:
NEW DELHI: With improvement in LPG supplies and a fall in refill backlogs, govt Monday reduced the minimum time gap for booking LPG refills in rural areas to 25 days from 45 days, bringing it on a par with the interval for urban consumers, reports Atul Mathur. Union minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi said the restriction had been imposed amid pressure on LPG supplies following the outbreak of the conflict in West Asia, with the booking interval set at 25 days in urban areas and 45 days in rural areas. "However, in view of the current LPG supply situation improving and the significant reduction in refill backlog, Centre has relaxed this restriction. Now, all domestic LPG consumers, regardless of urban or rural, can book refills at an interval of 25 days," Gopi said. Petroleum ministry has issued an order to oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL, asking them to implement this with immediate effect.
